description: §14.8.9 S441 fix round (F1) — the extracting helper lives in ANOTHER FILE (`helper.scrml` exports `pick(r) { return r.passwordHash }`; the entry imports it and returns `pick(u)`). The provenance flow analyses every server module of the compile with the imports between them resolved, so this is E-PROTECT-006 — and I-PROTECT-STRIP-001 does NOT claim a strip (the row never reached a redact sink).
rationale: MEASURED on the first S441 cut (g-protected-column-escapes-redaction-as-scalar, security review F1): the single-module analysis could not see into helper.server.js, so this compiled at exit 0, served HTTP 200 "SECRET-HASH-123", and still printed the false I-PROTECT-STRIP-001 "stripped" claim — the original defect's symptom, one file away. §14.8.9 (S441 amendment): "The analysis SHALL cover every server module the compile emits, with the imports between them resolved."
